findings.requirement: Storage/audit failures must propagate and roll back the entire transfer; existing trigger failures must not be bypassed.
findings.evidence: Initialize accounts ('one','a',100), ('one','b',0). Install: CREATE TRIGGER guard BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts WHEN NEW.balance=OLD.balance BEGIN SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.name='a' THEN RAISE(IGNORE) ELSE RAISE(ABORT,'blocked') END; END; CREATE TRIGGER audit_check AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance WHERE tenant=NEW.tenant; END; Call transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k'). The pre-repair version raises IntegrityError('blocked') and preserves all rows. The candidate returns success, durably commits balances 90/10 and creates both receipt and audit; CLI also exits 0. RAISE(IGNORE) skips the injected leave call, leaving a stale frame that suppresses the guard for the next row. Replacing RAISE(IGNORE) with NULL makes both versions correctly abort.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve native per-row trigger execution after RAISE(IGNORE). Ensure abandoned invocation state cannot suppress subsequent rows, and add the multirow abort case with its non-IGNORE control.

findings.requirement: Valid transfers must succeed while preserving compatible existing trigger behavior.
findings.evidence: Initialize accounts ('one','a',100), ('one','b',0), then install CREATE TRIGGER t AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN VALUES(1); END; Calling transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k') succeeds before repair but now raises IntegrityError('cannot observe storage effects'); CLI exits 2. SQLite accepts this harmless trigger. The same regression occurs with BEGIN WITH c AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM c; END. Both failures originate in the statement-prefix whitelist. Candidate rollback and trigger-definition preservation were verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Support SQLite-valid VALUES and WITH-prefixed SELECT trigger statements without changing their semantics. Add native-versus-instrumented compatibility checks for both forms.

checks: Read CONTRACT.md, local instructions and lean-run/write-integrity guidance; compared current source with .baseline and .pre-repair and inspected added tests.
Ran python3 -B -m unittest discover -v: all 37 tests passed on Python 3.14.3 / SQLite 3.50.4.
Independently confirmed rollback for erased audit rows, foreign balance changes, storage-class changes and extra UNIQUE-index REPLACE victims; stored rows and trigger definitions remained unchanged.
Confirmed harmless no-ops, ignored conflicts, rowid moves, malformed foreign TEXT and implicit REPLACE/total_changes controls succeed.
Confirmed escaped-equivalent duplicate JSON keys produce exit 2, empty stdout, generic stderr and no effects.
Confirmed durable replay after endpoint removal returns the original receipt without changes; fresh requests and conflicting payloads remain rejected.
Compared native and instrumented keyword/Unicode names, compound WHEN bodies, token-boundary BOM and embedded NBSP/BOM. Vertical tab and BOM appended to BEGIN were rejected by native SQLite.
Independently reproduced both findings through the public API and CLI, compared against .pre-repair, and inspected durable state after reopening.
Assessment made no persistent file changes; probes used temporary workspace paths and Python -B.
coverage_limits: Runtime verification covers the installed Python and SQLite versions only.
Trigger compatibility probes targeted the repair delta and demonstrated gaps; they do not exhaust SQLite trigger grammar or execution patterns.
